chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Musa, from 'Ali ibn Sa'id, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who was seized while digging up graves. He said: “I do not consider amputation to apply to him unless he is apprehended after having dug up graves repeatedly; then I would amputate him.”

As for what appears in the narration of 'Isa ibn Sabih and his statement, “The pickpocket, the grave-digger, and the snatcher are not subjected to amputation,” it is likely that something has fallen out of the report, because he narrated this very report itself and said: I asked him about these three, and he said: “The pickpocket and the grave-digger are subjected to amputation, while the snatcher is not subjected to amputation.”

We have already presented the narration from him concerning that. Had he not narrated this detailed clarification, we would have interpreted it according to the meaning on which we interpreted the last two reports that we discussed.

key_terms.التَّفْصِيلَ: the detailed clarification that resolves ambiguity
key_terms.النَّبَّاشُ: the grave-digger who exhumes graves unlawfully
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith text being discussed
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِسُ: the snatcher who seizes property openly and quickly
key_terms.قَطْعًا: amputation as the legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the grave-digger, pickpocket, and snatcher in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling concerning grave-digging and related forms of theft, distinguishing between cases that warrant amputation and those that do not. It also addresses an apparent contradiction in another narration and resolves it by preferring the more detailed report.
